title: Given the Pace of Change, Are Strategic Plans and Business Forecasts Still Useful or Even Necessary
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece questions whether traditional multi-year strategic plans still make sense given how quickly markets now shift. It argues planning retains value for clarity, not certainty, letting leaders test assumptions and explore scenarios even if the specific forecasts prove wrong. The article distinguishes a lofty, flexible organizational vision from rigid multi-year forecasts, suggesting the former still has value while the latter is increasingly obsolete. It recommends shifting to quarterly or monthly planning cycles to keep pace with change.
points: Traditional three-to-five-year strategic plans are increasingly obsolete given the pace of market change.
Planning's remaining value lies in clarity, not certainty — it helps leaders test assumptions.
Scenario planning across multiple plausible futures is recommended over single-point forecasts.
A broad organizational vision can remain valuable even as detailed forecasts lose relevance.
The article recommends quarterly or monthly planning cycles rather than long-range ones.
quotes: Traditional three-to-five-year strategic plans, which were once the mainstay of successful enterprises, are now laughable in their lack of utility.
Are leaders kidding themselves? Is strategic planning and forecasting in today’s world a wasteful exercise?
For the best teams and organizations, strategic planning continues to be an essential process for reasons of clarity, not certainty.
Good visions depend less on forecasts and predictions and more on what the organization desires to become regardless of the environment.
Those who expect more will make fortune tellers and palm readers look good.
